en: The Questions of Milinda: The Section on the Refutation of Difficulties (Meṇḍakapañha),
Chapter on What is Set Aside (Paṇāmitavagga)
9. The Question on the Foremost Ascetic “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Through the destruction of the taints, one becomes an ascetic (samaṇa).’”
And again it was said:
“One who is endowed with four qualities,
him indeed they call a recluse in the world.”
In this regard, these four qualities are patience, moderation in food, the relinquishing of delight, and nothingness.
However, all of these belong only to one whose taints (*āsava*) are not yet exhausted and who still possesses defilements (*sakilesa*).

If, venerable Nāgasena, one becomes a recluse through the destruction of the taints, then the statement that “the person endowed with these four qualities is indeed called a recluse in the world” must be false.

“If a recluse is one who possesses four qualities, then the statement that ‘one becomes a recluse through the destruction of the taints’ must be false. This too is a dilemma with two horns that has come upon you; it must be resolved by you.
“Great King, this was indeed spoken by the Blessed One: ‘One becomes a recluse through the destruction of the taints.
And yet, it was also said:”
"One who is endowed with four qualities, him indeed they call a recluse in the world"—this statement, Great King, was spoken in reference to the specific virtues of certain individuals:
"One who is endowed with four qualities, him indeed they call a recluse in the world. But this is an exhaustive statement: "Through the destruction of the taints, one becomes a recluse."
Moreover, Great King, whoever has set out for the pacification of the defilements, among them all, the ascetic whose taints are destroyed is declared to be the foremost.
Just as, Great King, whatever flowers there may be—whether born of water or born of land—the *vassika* is declared to be the foremost;
though there are various other kinds of flowers, they are all merely flowers, and [the *vassika* is supreme] among them all.
But the *vassika* flower alone is desired and longed for by the people;
even so, Great King, among all those who have set out for the pacification of the defilements, the ascetic whose taints are destroyed is declared to be the foremost, surpassing them all.

Or again, Great King, just as among all grains rice is declared to be the foremost, and whatever other various kinds of grain there may be, they are all used as food to sustain the body, yet rice alone is declared to be the best among them; even so, Great King, among all those who have set out for the pacification of the defilements, the ascetic whose taints are destroyed is declared to be the foremost, surpassing them all.
"In the very same way, Great King, whoever has set out for the pacification of the defilements, among them all, the monk who has destroyed the taints is declared to be the foremost.
"Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! It is so; I accept it as such.
Thus ends the ninth dilemma: The Foremost Monk.
